question: On Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how many free looks (safe exits to check the vehicle's position) is a driver allowed?
choice_a: One (1) free look
choice_b: Two (2) free looks
choice_c: Three (3) free looks
choice_d: No free looks are allowed
explanation: The manual states a driver may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: On Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how many free looks is a driver allowed to check the vehicle's position?
choice_a: One (1) free look
choice_b: Two (2) free looks
choice_c: Three (3) free looks
choice_d: Four (4) free looks
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Looks

question: "Final Position" is scored during the Basic Control Skills test on which two exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 and Exercise 3
choice_b: Exercise 1 and Exercise 4
choice_c: Exercise 2 and Exercise 4
choice_d: Exercise 3 only
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Final Position

question: What must a driver do upon completion of a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and honk the horn twice
choice_b: Set the parking brake, turn on the hazard lights, and sound the horn
choice_c: Shift to neutral/park, sound the horn, and open the door to check position
choice_d: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
explanation: Upon completion of an exercise, the driver must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate the exercise is complete.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Exercise Completion Procedure

question: What happens if a driver does not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner?
choice_a: The driver will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: The driver will simply receive a warning and continue
choice_c: The driver will be given one additional free look to correct it
choice_d: Only points on pull-ups will be affected
explanation: The manual states that failing to maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described will result in a penalty and failure of the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Final Position

question: What may cause an automatic failure and termination of the Basic Control Skills test related to examiner instructions?
choice_a: Braking smoothly at a stop sign
choice_b: Failure to follow examiner instructions for completing an exercise as directed
choice_c: Asking the examiner for clarification
choice_d: Checking traffic before a turn
explanation: The manual states that failure to follow examiner instructions for completing an exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act

question: Which of the following is given as an example of an "unsafe act" that may result in automatic failure during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Sounding the horn after completing an exercise
choice_b: Asking to be walked through the exercise area
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while the vehicle is in motion
choice_d: Pulling straight forward past the alley entrance when signaled by the examiner
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of an unsafe act that may result in automatic failure.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act

question: What does the manual say a driver should do if they do not understand the examiner's instructions for an exercise?
choice_a: Guess and proceed with the exercise
choice_b: Exit the vehicle without permission to look around
choice_c: Skip that exercise and move to the next one
choice_d: Ask the examiner for clarification
explanation: The manual instructs drivers who do not understand the instructions or how to complete an exercise to ask the examiner for clarification.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act

question: What does Exercise 1 - Forward Stop require the driver to do?
choice_a: Drive forward through the alley and stop with the front-most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it
choice_b: Back through the alley and stop within three feet of the rear boundary
choice_c: Drive forward and steer left through an opening without stopping
choice_d: Parallel park within a marked stall
explanation: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop requires the driver to judge the front of the vehicle and stop with the front-most part within the box at the end of the alley without going past it.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: During Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may the driver stop?
choice_a: As many times as needed
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: Twice, with one free look
choice_d: The driver must not stop until instructed by the examiner
explanation: The manual states you may stop only once during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: After stopping during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately exit the vehicle to check position
choice_b: Turn on the four-way flashers
choice_c: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_d: Pull forward past the stop box
explanation: When stopped, the driver must set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what happens if the front-most part of the vehicle is not within the stop box?
choice_a: The exercise is automatically failed with no scoring
choice_b: Nothing, since only encroachments are scored
choice_c: The exercise must be repeated
choice_d: The driver will be scored for the front-most part of the vehicle not being in the stop box
explanation: The manual states the driver will receive points (be scored) if the front-most part of the vehicle is not in the stop box.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: Who points out the front-most part of the vehicle before Exercise 1 - Forward Stop begins?
choice_a: The examiner, when giving instructions for the exercise
choice_b: The driver decides independently
choice_c: It is marked on the pavement with paint
choice_d: A second CDL examiner riding along
explanation: The manual states the examiner will point out the front-most part of the vehicle when giving instructions for this exercise.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, when does the examiner signal you to begin backing?
choice_a: Immediately upon entering the vehicle
choice_b: After you pull forward and stop when the examiner raises their hand
choice_c: After completing three practice loops
choice_d: Only after Exercise 4 is finished
explanation: From the stopped position of the previous exercise, the examiner asks the driver to pull forward and stop when they raise their hand, then back straight through the alley.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How far must the driver back during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Until the rear of the vehicle reaches the alley entrance
choice_b: Exactly 50 feet
choice_c: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
choice_d: Until signaled by a spotter outside the vehicle
explanation: The driver must back straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing is scored for which of the following?
choice_a: Speed, steering angle, and clutch usage
choice_b: Turn signal use and mirror checks only
choice_c: Lane usage and braking only
choice_d: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free pull-up
choice_b: Two (2) free pull-ups
choice_c: Three (3) free pull-ups
choice_d: No free pull-ups are allowed
explanation: The manual states the driver is allowed one free pull-up during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: During Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how many times may the driver safely exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: Two times
choice_b: Only one time
choice_c: Three times
choice_d: As many times as needed within the time limit
explanation: The manual states the driver may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What must a driver do upon completing Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing to inform the examiner?
choice_a: Flash the headlights twice
choice_b: Roll down the window and announce completion
choice_c: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_d: Activate the four-way emergency flashers
explanation: Completion is signaled by setting the parking brake, shifting to neutral/park, and sounding the horn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What does Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking test the driver's ability to do?
choice_a: Back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_b: Parallel park within boundary lines
choice_c: Execute a precise controlled forward stop
choice_d: Maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping
explanation: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking demonstrates the driver's ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: During Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, which direction does the driver steer through the opening into the opposite lane?
choice_a: Left
choice_b: Right
choice_c: Either direction, driver's choice
choice_d: The exercise requires only braking, not steering
explanation: The driver drives forward and steers to the left through the opening into the opposite lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what must the driver keep between the cone and the line?
choice_a: The front bumper
choice_b: The right-most rear tire
choice_c: The left-most rear tire
choice_d: The trailer landing gear
explanation: The driver must keep the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking is scored for which of the following?
choice_a: Pull-ups and final position
choice_b: Looks and parking brake usage
choice_c: Encroachments and forward tracking clearance
choice_d: Turn signal timing and gear selection
explanation: The manual states the driver will be scored for encroachments and forward tracking clearance (rear tire between the cone and the line).
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What happens if a driver stops, backs up, or exits the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: The driver receives one free pull-up
choice_b: The driver is scored a "look" only
choice_c: Nothing, these actions are permitted
choice_d: These actions are not allowed, and if the driver stops, the exercise will be ended
explanation: The manual states the driver is not allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during this exercise, and stopping ends the exercise.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Where must the driver stop the vehicle at the end of Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Parallel to the outer boundary and prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise
choice_b: Anywhere within three feet of the rear boundary
choice_c: At the point where the examiner raises a hand mid-maneuver
choice_d: Past the final set of cones, then backed up to align
explanation: The driver stops the vehicle when parallel to the outer boundary and prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What does Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing require the driver to demonstrate?
choice_a: Driving forward through a narrow alley without stopping
choice_b: Offset backing and parking a vehicle at the end of an alley
choice_c: Executing a controlled stop at a marked box
choice_d: Merging into expressway traffic
explanation: Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing demonstrates the driver's ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close to the rear of the alley must the rear-most part of the vehicle come?
choice_a: Within ten (10) feet
choice_b: Within one (1) foot
choice_c: Within three (3) feet
choice_d: Touching the rear boundary line exactly
explanation: The driver must offset back, bringing the rear-most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: If a driver backs beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, what must they do?
choice_a: Immediately fail the exercise with no recovery
choice_b: Continue backing until instructed otherwise
choice_c: Exit the vehicle to reposition manually
choice_d: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, before resuming the exercise
explanation: The manual instructs that if you back beyond the rear boundary, you must pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing is scored for which of the following?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_b: Speed control and clutch usage only
choice_c: Turn signals and lane usage
choice_d: Braking distance and steering angle
explanation: The manual states the driver will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on Exercise 4.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free pull-up
choice_b: Two (2) free pull-ups
choice_c: Three (3) free pull-ups
choice_d: No free pull-ups
explanation: The manual states the driver is allowed two free pull-ups during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: During Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how many times may the driver exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: Only one time
choice_b: Three times
choice_c: A maximum of two times
choice_d: An unlimited number of times
explanation: The manual states the driver may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be true of the vehicle's position within the alley when Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing is completed?
choice_a: It may be angled up to 15 degrees
choice_b: It must be touching the outer boundary line
choice_c: It must be positioned diagonally to maximize visibility
choice_d: It must be straight within the alley and completely within the defined exercise boundaries
explanation: The manual requires the vehicle to be straight within the alley and completely within the defined exercise boundaries when the exercise is completed.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is required of the driver at all times?
choice_a: Wearing your safety belt
choice_b: Keeping the radio off
choice_c: Driving with hazard lights on
choice_d: Using cruise control whenever possible
explanation: The manual requires the driver to wear their safety belt at all times during the on-road driving test.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: During the on-road driving test, the examiner scores the driver on what two things?
choice_a: Fuel efficiency and total time
choice_b: Specific driving maneuvers and general driving behavior
choice_c: Passenger comfort and route memorization
choice_d: Vehicle appearance and paperwork accuracy
explanation: The examiner scores the driver on specific driving maneuvers as well as general driving behavior.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask the driver to do?
choice_a: Skip that portion of the test entirely
choice_b: Drive to a different route
choice_c: Simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing
choice_d: Automatically receive full credit for that maneuver
explanation: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the driver may be asked to simulate them by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: To pass the on-road driving test, the driver must complete the test without which of the following?
choice_a: Using turn signals
choice_b: Changing gears
choice_c: Checking mirrors
choice_d: An accident or moving violation
explanation: The driver must complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: Before making a turn, what must a driver do first?
choice_a: Check traffic in all directions
choice_b: Immediately apply the brake
choice_c: Downshift two gears
choice_d: Signal after beginning the turn
explanation: When asked to make a turn, the driver must first check traffic in all directions before using signals and moving into the needed lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: According to the manual, when does "unsafe coasting" occur?
choice_a: Whenever a driver shifts gears near a turn
choice_b: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_c: When speed exceeds the posted limit
choice_d: Whenever the driver uses the clutch to shift
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as the vehicle being out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If a driver must stop before making a turn, how should the stop be made?
choice_a: With a hard brake application
choice_b: While skidding, if intentional
choice_c: A smooth stop without skidding, behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign
choice_d: Anywhere within the intersection
explanation: The manual states the driver should come to a smooth stop without skidding, behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While actually making a turn, what should the driver do with their hands?
choice_a: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the gearshift
choice_b: Take both hands off the wheel while checking mirrors
choice_c: Keep one hand on the turn signal at all times
choice_d: Keep both hands on the steering wheel during the turn
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep both hands on the steering wheel during the turn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While turning, the driver should keep checking the mirror to make sure of what?
choice_a: The vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
choice_b: The trailer brake light is functioning
choice_c: No vehicle is following too closely
choice_d: The turn signal has automatically canceled
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep checking the mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: After completing a turn, the driver should move into which lane when safe to do so (if not already there)?
choice_a: The center lane
choice_b: The right-most lane
choice_c: The left-most lane
choice_d: Whichever lane has the least traffic, regardless of position
explanation: After the turn, the driver should get up to speed of traffic, use the turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: Where should the vehicle finish a turn, according to the Turns guidance?
choice_a: In the lane closest to the shoulder, regardless of turn direction
choice_b: In any open lane
choice_c: In the correct lane, without moving into oncoming traffic
choice_d: Straddling two lanes briefly before merging
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should not move into oncoming traffic and should finish the turn in the correct lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As a driver approaches an intersection, what should they do regarding speed and braking?
choice_a: Maintain current speed until the stop line
choice_b: Accelerate to clear the intersection quickly
choice_c: Come to a complete stop immediately regardless of the signal
choice_d: Decelerate gently and brake smoothly, changing gears if necessary
explanation: As you approach an intersection, you should decelerate gently and brake smoothly, changing gears if necessary.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: At an intersection requiring a stop, what must the driver avoid doing while stopped?
choice_a: Rolling the vehicle forward or backward
choice_b: Using the parking brake
choice_c: Checking traffic in all directions
choice_d: Maintaining a safe gap behind the vehicle ahead
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must not roll forward or backward while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what must the driver do regarding lane changes?
choice_a: Change lanes freely if traffic allows
choice_b: Not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Change lanes only to the right
choice_d: Change lanes only if signaled by another driver
explanation: The manual states the driver should not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, the driver must decelerate and yield to what?
choice_a: Oncoming left-turning vehicles only
choice_b: Vehicles behind them
choice_c: Any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection
choice_d: Cyclists only, not pedestrians
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to decelerate and yield to any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: Once through an intersection, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately change lanes to pass slower traffic
choice_b: Turn off traffic checks until the next intersection
choice_c: Coast until reaching normal speed
choice_d: Continue checking mirrors and traffic while accelerating smoothly and changing gears as necessary
explanation: Once through the intersection, the driver should continue checking mirrors and traffic, and accelerate smoothly, changing gears as necessary.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: When stopping at an intersection with no vehicle ahead, where should the driver stop?
choice_a: Behind the stop sign, signal, sidewalk, or stop line
choice_b: As close to the crosswalk as physically possible, even if over the line
choice_c: At least one full car length past the stop line for visibility
choice_d: Wherever gives the best view, regardless of markings
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to come to a complete stop behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: If stopping behind another vehicle at an intersection, where should the driver stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Bumper to bumper with the vehicle ahead
choice_b: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_c: At least three vehicle lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_d: Wherever is convenient; gap distance is not addressed
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you for a safe gap.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should the vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Straddling the right-most and center lanes
choice_b: In the left-most lane to allow faster traffic to pass
choice_c: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane)
choice_d: As close to parked cars as possible
explanation: During the Urban Business portion, the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane, which is the right-most lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: Regarding speed during the Urban Business portion of the test, the driver should do what?
choice_a: Always drive 5 mph under the posted limit
choice_b: Match the fastest vehicle on the road
choice_c: Ignore the posted speed limit if traffic is moving faster
choice_d: Keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit during Urban Business driving.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, what following distance behavior is expected of the driver?
choice_a: Maintain a safe following distance
choice_b: Tailgate slightly to discourage lane changes by others
choice_c: Following distance is not evaluated in this segment
choice_d: Maintain exactly one car length regardless of speed
explanation: The manual states the driver is expected to make regular traffic checks and maintain a safe following distance during the Urban Business portion.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: During the lane change portion of the test, what direction changes will the driver be asked to make?
choice_a: Right only
choice_b: Change lanes to the left, then back to the right
choice_c: Diagonal changes across multiple lanes at once
choice_d: U-turns within the lane
explanation: During multiple lane portions of the test, the driver will be asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Before changing lanes during the test, what must the driver do first?
choice_a: Increase speed to create a gap
choice_b: Turn on the hazard lights
choice_c: Make the necessary traffic checks
choice_d: Honk the horn to alert nearby drivers
explanation: The driver should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: When should a driver change lanes during the lane change portion of the test?
choice_a: As quickly as possible to avoid holding up traffic
choice_b: Only when directed by a passenger
choice_c: At a fixed point marked on the route
choice_d: Smoothly, when it is safe to do so, after signaling
explanation: After making traffic checks and signaling, the driver should smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Before entering the expressway, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane
choice_b: Come to a complete stop at the entrance ramp
choice_c: Downshift to the lowest gear
choice_d: Activate the four-way flashers
explanation: Before entering the expressway, the driver must check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the expressway, what must the driver maintain?
choice_a: Only vehicle speed; spacing is not addressed
choice_b: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_c: Maximum legal speed at all times
choice_d: The left-most lane exclusively
explanation: Once on the expressway, the driver must maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, once on the exit ramp, what must the driver continue to do?
choice_a: Accelerate to merge back if needed
choice_b: Turn off the turn signal immediately
choice_c: Decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between vehicles
choice_d: Change lanes to find the fastest route off the ramp
explanation: Once on the exit ramp, the driver must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between the vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, what must the driver do before decelerating in the exit lane?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop first
choice_b: Turn off the headlights
choice_c: Shift into neutral
choice_d: Make necessary traffic checks and use proper signals
explanation: When exiting the expressway, the driver must make necessary traffic checks and use proper signals before decelerating smoothly in the exit lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, what is the driver asked to simulate?
choice_a: Pulling over to the side of the road as if to get out and check something on the vehicle
choice_b: A complete engine shutdown and restart
choice_c: A railroad crossing stop
choice_d: An emergency evasive stop
explanation: For this maneuver, the driver is asked to pull the vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if going to get out and check something on the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: As you prepare for the Stop/Start maneuver stop, which turn signal should be activated?
choice_a: Left turn signal
choice_b: Right turn signal
choice_c: Both turn signals simultaneously
choice_d: No turn signal is required
explanation: As you prepare for the stop, you check traffic and activate your right turn signal.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, how must the vehicle be positioned relative to the curb or shoulder?
choice_a: At a 45-degree angle for visibility
choice_b: At least two feet away from the curb
choice_c: Parallel to the curb or shoulder and safely out of the traffic flow
choice_d: Straddling the fog line
explanation: Once stopped, the vehicle must be parallel to the curb or shoulder of the road and safely out of the traffic flow.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once stopped, the vehicle should not be blocking which of the following?
choice_a: Only fire hydrants
choice_b: Only other parked vehicles
choice_c: Nothing in particular; blocking is not scored
choice_d: Driveways, fire hydrants, intersections, signs, etc.
explanation: The vehicle should not be blocking driveways, fire hydrants, intersections, signs, etc. once stopped.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, besides applying the parking brake, what else must the driver do?
choice_a: Activate the four-way emergency flashers and move the gear shift to neutral or park
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Open the driver's door to check traffic
choice_d: Sound the horn three times
explanation: Once stopped, the driver must cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: While stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, where should the driver's feet be?
choice_a: Held firmly on the brake pedal
choice_b: Removed from the brake and clutch pedals
choice_c: Resting on the accelerator
choice_d: Positioned to allow a quick emergency start
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to remove their feet from the brake and clutch pedals once stopped.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, after checking traffic and mirrors and turning off the four-way flashers, which turn signal should be activated?
choice_a: Right turn signal
choice_b: No turn signal is needed
choice_c: Left turn signal
choice_d: Hazard flashers should stay on
explanation: When instructed to resume, the driver turns off the four-way flashers and activates the left turn signal before pulling back into traffic.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, what must the driver avoid doing before the vehicle moves?
choice_a: Checking traffic to the left
choice_b: Releasing the parking brake
choice_c: Canceling the turn signal
choice_d: Turning the wheel before the vehicle moves
explanation: The manual instructs that the driver should not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves when resuming from the stop.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should the driver reduce speed?
choice_a: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: While already inside the curve
choice_c: Only after exiting the curve
choice_d: Speed reduction is not addressed for curves
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to reduce speed before entering the curve so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: While driving through a curve, what must the driver do with the vehicle?
choice_a: Straddle the center line for a wider turning radius
choice_b: Keep the vehicle in the lane
choice_c: Accelerate through to maintain momentum
choice_d: Brake continuously through the curve
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep the vehicle in the lane while driving through a curve.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before entering a curve, along with reducing speed, what else should the driver do?
choice_a: Downshift to first gear regardless of speed
choice_b: Activate the four-way flashers
choice_c: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_d: Come to a complete stop
explanation: When approaching a curve, the driver should check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before reaching a railroad crossing, all commercial drivers should do which of the following?
choice_a: Accelerate to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_b: Change lanes to get the best view of the tracks
choice_c: Shift into neutral to coast across
choice_d: Decelerate, brake smoothly, and shift gears as necessary
explanation: Before reaching the crossing, all commercial drivers should decelerate, brake smoothly, and shift gears as necessary.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, all commercial drivers must not do which of the following?
choice_a: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_b: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
choice_c: Look and listen for trains
choice_d: Check traffic in all directions
explanation: The manual states drivers must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For drivers of a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, when should the four-way flashers be activated relative to a railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt)?
choice_a: Only after fully crossing the tracks
choice_b: As the vehicle approaches the railroad crossing
choice_c: Flashers are not required for railroad crossings
choice_d: Only if a train is visibly approaching
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, the driver should activate the four-way flashers.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle, within what distance range from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_b: Within 100 feet but not less than 30 feet
choice_c: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states the driver should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: At a railroad crossing, a bus driver may also be required to do what before crossing the tracks?
choice_a: Turn off the engine and restart it
choice_b: Exit the vehicle to inspect the tracks
choice_c: Radio dispatch for clearance
choice_d: Open the window and door prior to crossing tracks
explanation: The manual states that if operating a bus, the driver may also be required to open the window and door prior to crossing the tracks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: While a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle is proceeding across railroad tracks, where should the driver's hands be?
choice_a: Kept on the steering wheel
choice_b: One hand on the horn at all times
choice_c: Ready to shift gears as needed
choice_d: Free to adjust the mirrors
explanation: The manual states the driver should keep hands on the steering wheel as the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle crosses railroad tracks, when should the four-way flashers be deactivated?
choice_a: They should remain on for the rest of the route
choice_b: After the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_c: Before entering the crossing
choice_d: Only if instructed by dispatch
explanation: The manual states the four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: Because not all road test routes include a railroad crossing, what may a driver be asked to do instead?
choice_a: Automatically fail that portion
choice_b: Skip railroad crossing knowledge entirely
choice_c: Explain and demonstrate the proper railroad crossing procedures to the examiner at a simulated location
choice_d: Drive to the nearest known crossing regardless of the route
explanation: The manual states that if the route lacks a railroad crossing, the driver may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper procedures at a simulated location.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For all commercial drivers approaching a railroad crossing (not just bus or placarded vehicle drivers), what must they do besides decelerating and braking smoothly?
choice_a: Activate the stop arm
choice_b: Open the door to listen
choice_c: Turn on the amber warning lights
choice_d: Look and listen for the presence of trains, and check traffic in all directions
explanation: All commercial drivers should look and listen for the presence of trains and check traffic in all directions before reaching a railroad crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the test, what may the driver be asked?
choice_a: What the posted clearance or height was
choice_b: What the speed limit under the overpass was
choice_c: How many support columns the overpass had
choice_d: What year the overpass was built
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge during the test, what may the driver be asked?
choice_a: The bridge's total length
choice_b: What the posted weight limit was
choice_c: The number of lanes on the bridge
choice_d: The name of the waterway below
explanation: After going over a bridge, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: If the test route does not include a bridge or overpass, what may the driver be asked about instead?
choice_a: A railroad crossing simulation only
choice_b: A parallel parking maneuver
choice_c: Another traffic sign, and be prepared to identify and explain it
choice_d: Nothing; the topic is simply skipped
explanation: If the route does not have a bridge or overpass, the driver may be asked about another traffic sign and should be prepared to identify and explain any sign on the route.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: To demonstrate a student discharge, what endorsement must the driver be applying for?
choice_a: Passenger (P) endorsement
choice_b: Tank vehicle (N) endorsement
choice_c: Hazardous materials (H) endorsement
choice_d: School Bus (S) endorsement
explanation: The manual states that if applying for a School Bus endorsement, the driver will be required to demonstrate a student discharge.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pickup for a school bus discharge, what warning lights and signals must be activated?
choice_a: Amber warning lights and right turn signals
choice_b: Red warning lights and left turn signals
choice_c: Four-way emergency flashers only
choice_d: Headlights and high beams
explanation: As you approach the student pickup, the manual instructs the driver to activate amber warning lights and right turn signals.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pickup, where should the school bus move on the traveled portion of the roadway?
choice_a: Into the center of the road for visibility
choice_b: As far as possible to the right
choice_c: Onto the shoulder only if it is paved
choice_d: Into the opposing lane if it is clear
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to move as far as possible to the right on the traveled portion of the roadway when approaching the student pickup.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When stopping for a student discharge, how far away from the students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 25 feet away
choice_b: At least 5 feet away
choice_c: At least 10 feet away
choice_d: Exactly at the curb, with no minimum distance specified
explanation: The manual requires the school bus to come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When stopped for a student discharge, besides setting the parking brake and placing the transmission in neutral/park, what must the driver activate?
choice_a: The headlights and hazard flashers
choice_b: The right turn signal only
choice_c: The horn, sounded once
choice_d: The stop arm and red warning lights
explanation: As you stop for the student discharge, you must place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When discharging students from a school bus, what must the driver do regarding the door?
choice_a: Open the student door after checking traffic and communicating to students
choice_b: Keep the door closed until students knock
choice_c: Open the door before coming to a complete stop
choice_d: Have a second adult open the door
explanation: When discharging students, the driver must communicate to students, check traffic, open the student door, and check for students.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When students are crossing in front of the school bus, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately close the door for safety
choice_b: Check traffic, communicate to students, and check for students
choice_c: Turn off the stop arm before students finish crossing
choice_d: Begin to slowly move forward to save time
explanation: When students are crossing, the driver must check traffic, communicate to students, and check for students.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When resuming from a student discharge, what must the driver do after checking all mirrors?
choice_a: Immediately accelerate away
choice_b: Sound the horn to alert students
choice_c: Turn off the warning lights and stop arm, then close the door
choice_d: Reactivate the amber warning lights
explanation: When resuming from the student discharge, the driver must check all mirrors, turn off the warning lights and stop arm, close the door, check traffic, and accelerate away.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: The "General Driving Behaviors" scoring categories in Section 13 include which of the following areas?
choice_a: Fuel economy and idle time
choice_b: Passenger comfort ratings
choice_c: Route familiarity
choice_d: Clutch usage, gear usage, brake usage, lane usage, steering, traffic checks, and use of turn signals
explanation: The manual scores overall performance in general driving behavior categories including clutch usage, gear usage, brake usage, lane usage, steering, regular traffic checks, and use of turn signals.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11 General Driving Behaviors

question: On a manual transmission vehicle, what must the driver always use to shift?
choice_a: The clutch
choice_b: The accelerator only
choice_c: Engine braking alone
choice_d: RPM matching without the clutch
explanation: The manual states that a driver must always use the clutch to shift on a manual transmission vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: If equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, what technique must the driver use when shifting?
choice_a: Float the gears without using the clutch
choice_b: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_c: Single-clutch with an extended pause in neutral
choice_d: Use the parking brake to assist gear changes
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which of the following is explicitly prohibited regarding clutch usage?
choice_a: Double-clutching an unsynchronized transmission
choice_b: Using the clutch to shift gears
choice_c: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_d: Returning both hands to the wheel after shifting
explanation: The manual prohibits riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or popping the clutch.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Besides not riding the clutch, what else must a manual-transmission driver avoid?
choice_a: Idling at a complete stop
choice_b: Using engine braking on a downgrade
choice_c: Shifting while going straight
choice_d: Revving or lugging the engine
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to rev or lug the engine when shifting on a manual transmission.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Regarding gear usage on a manual transmission, what is a driver instructed not to do?
choice_a: Grind or clash gears
choice_b: Select a gear that avoids revving the engine
choice_c: Use the clutch when shifting
choice_d: Shift while driving straight
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to grind or clash gears.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: According to Gear Usage guidance, when should a driver avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: On expressways
choice_b: In turns and intersections
choice_c: Before a railroad crossing
choice_d: While stopped at a red light
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What gear should a driver select according to the Gear Usage guidance?
choice_a: The lowest gear available at all times
choice_b: The highest gear for fuel economy
choice_c: A gear that does not rev or lug the engine
choice_d: Whatever gear matches the posted speed limit exactly
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Regarding brake usage, what is a driver instructed not to do?
choice_a: Brake smoothly using steady pressure
choice_b: Brake before entering a curve
choice_c: Brake at intersections
choice_d: Ride or pump the brake
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to ride or pump the brake.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: How should a driver apply the brakes according to Brake Usage guidance?
choice_a: Smoothly, using steady pressure, without braking harshly
choice_b: With quick, hard pumps for maximum stopping power
choice_c: Only when the vehicle ahead brakes first
choice_d: With the parking brake engaged for extra control
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to brake harshly and to brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: Regarding lane usage, what is a driver instructed not to put the vehicle over?
choice_a: The centerline only
choice_b: Curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings
choice_c: Speed bumps
choice_d: Crosswalk paint only
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to put the vehicle over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Where must a driver stop according to Lane Usage guidance?
choice_a: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_b: At the driver's discretion based on visibility
choice_c: Behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs
choice_d: In the crosswalk if traffic allows
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: On a multiple lane road, where should a vehicle finish a left turn?
choice_a: In the left-most lane available
choice_b: In any lane going the correct direction
choice_c: Straddling two lanes until traffic clears
choice_d: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Where should a vehicle finish a right turn?
choice_a: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_b: In the lane closest to the center line
choice_c: In whichever lane has less traffic
choice_d: In a lane at least one lane away from the curb
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Unless a lane is blocked, where should a driver move to or remain?
choice_a: The center lane
choice_b: The right-most lane
choice_c: The left-most lane
choice_d: Whichever lane matches the fastest traffic flow
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to move to or remain in the right-most lane unless the lane is blocked.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Regarding steering, what is a driver instructed to avoid?
choice_a: Using both hands on the wheel
choice_b: Returning hands to the wheel after shifting
choice_c: Over or under steering the vehicle
choice_d: Checking mirrors while steering
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to over or under steer the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: According to the Steering guidance, when may a driver's hands leave the steering wheel?
choice_a: While approaching an intersection
choice_b: While making a turn
choice_c: Hands should never leave the wheel under any circumstance
choice_d: Only while shifting, after which both hands must return to the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, returning both hands after the shift is complete.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: According to Regular Traffic Checks guidance, when should mirrors and traffic be checked relative to an intersection?
choice_a: Before, while in, and after the intersection
choice_b: Only before entering
choice_c: Only while stopped
choice_d: Only after passing through
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to check mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: Where should a driver scan and check traffic with extra attention, per Regular Traffic Checks guidance?
choice_a: Only on expressways
choice_b: High volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present
choice_c: Only in rural areas
choice_d: Only near railroad crossings
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to scan and check traffic in high volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: When must a driver cancel their turn signal, per Use of Turn Signals guidance?
choice_a: Immediately upon activating it
choice_b: Only when the examiner instructs
choice_c: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_d: Turn signals cancel automatically and require no driver action
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals

question: According to Use of Turn Signals guidance, in addition to using signals properly and canceling them after use, what else is required?
choice_a: Signals must be checked before the test begins
choice_b: Signals must flash at least twice
choice_c: Signals must be manually canceled by the examiner
choice_d: Activating turn signals at appropriate times and when required
explanation: The manual requires the driver to activate turn signals when required and at appropriate times, in addition to using and canceling them properly.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals
